svg.title: Binding energy per nucleon
svg.desc: Average binding energy per nucleon, BE/A in MeV, versus mass number A for stable nuclei. It rises steeply from 1.1 MeV for ²H, with a spike at ⁴He (7.07 MeV) above ⁶Li and ⁷Li, to a broad peak of about 8.8 MeV near A = 60 (⁵⁶Fe and ⁶²Ni), then falls slowly to 7.6 MeV at ²³⁸U as Coulomb repulsion grows. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: A bound nucleus has less rest mass than its separate nucleons
BE = (m p + m n − m D)c²
Mass energies are in MeV. Binding releases 2.225 MeV in the zero-input-kinetic-energy limit, shared
by photon and recoil. The wave symbol marks radiation, not a calculated photon path.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
